title: (How) Do MLLMs Report Bistable Images Like Humans?
abstract: arXiv:2609.13254v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Bistable images such as the duck-rabbit are classic stimuli in which one image supports multiple mutually incompatible interpretations, typically reported one at a time in humans. We ask whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show similar report behavior and what internal computations support it. Using the LLaVA family, we study two tractable dimensions: modulability, whether reports can be biased by bottom-up visual cues and top-down linguistic priors, and exclusivity, whether responses commit to a single interpretation. We test both on the canonical duck-rabbit and on synthetic Visual Anagrams to mitigate memorization confounds. Behaviorally, both visual and linguistic manipulations systematically shift reports in human-consistent ways, while responses remain predominantly exclusive. translated_title: 多模态大语言模型如何像人类一样报告双稳态图像？
translated_abstract: 双稳态图像（如经典的鸭兔图）是指一幅图像支持多种互不相容的解释，而人类通常一次只报告其中一种。我们探究多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）是否表现出类似的报告行为，以及是何种内部计算机制在支持这种行为。我们以LLaVA系列模型为研究对象，从两个可操作的维度展开研究：可调性，即模型报告能否被自下而上的视觉线索和自上而下的语言先验所偏置；排他性，即模型的响应是否仅承诺单一解释。我们在经典的鸭兔图以及合成的视觉字谜上进行测试，以缓解记忆效应带来的混淆。在行为层面，视觉和语言操纵都能以与人类一致的方式系统性地改变模型的报告，而响应则主要保持排他性。在机制层面，这些效应源于图像标记表征之间的竞争、自下而上与自上而下调节所经过的不同通路……
tldr: 研究发现多模态大语言模型（如LLaVA）在解读鸭兔图等双稳态图像时表现出与人类相似的行为——其报告可被视觉线索和语言先验系统性调制且保持解释排他性，其内在机制源于图像标记表征间的竞争。
en_tdlr: MLLMs like LLaVA report bistable images in human-like ways—their interpretations can be systematically modulated by visual cues and linguistic priors while remaining exclusive—driven internally by competition between image-token representations.
